name: Enabling
leftDef: Enabling: Promotes flexibility, communication, and fostering autonomy by creating a safe, developmental environment. Leaders actively listen and encourage diverse perspectives. They promote autonomy and provide the freedom to act, encouraging innovation through facilitative and enabling leadership that values co-creation. Leaders focus on active listening and creating safe spaces where challenge is encouraged and collaboration is prioritized.
rightDef: Disempowering: Command-and-control approach that is leader-focused and stifles innovation and collaboration. Authoritarian, hierarchical, and often driven by predetermined outcomes or rigid job boundaries. Limits participation and autonomy in order to maintain and retain leadership control. Foster an environment of fear, anxiety, and judgment. The emphasis is on compliance and performance management.

name: Transformational
leftDef: Transformational: Long-term, strategic thinking, encourages disruptive innovation. Leaders think differently and challenge conventional approaches, seeking new ways of working and doing things differently. Proactive, fostering a culture which encourages risk taking to achieve sustainable improvements. Visionary thinking, pushing for strategic innovations. Open to change and focus on long-term goals.
rightDef: Transactional: Focus on maintaining the status quo and achieving short-term objectives. This leadership style is rigid, with leaders relying on established rules and procedures, avoiding change and innovation. Task orientated, risk averse, resistant to change, short-term focused and promoted limited engagement where leaders prioritise compliance over creativity.
quote: "Constraining and stifles creativity and innovation", "Yeah, prepared to look at change and new ways of working, new ways of doing things. The other was about keeping maintaining t

name: Collective
leftDef: Collective: Facilitates shared leadership responsibility and accountability, and inclusive participation where stakeholders influence. Leaders invest time to co-develop solutions, fostering collective ownership and mutual accountability, valuing equal contributions. Transparent decision-making, non-judgmental, and vision-led, with a focus on long-term, system-wide improvements. Values collective wisdom and builds consensus.
rightDef: Individualistic: Focuses on individual or organizational gain, prioritiszing quick wins and personal success over collective goals. Solutions are pre-determined and imposed through authority, limiting broader participation. Decision-making is transactional, opaque, and driven by a narrow focus on immediate outcomes. Leadership tends to allocate blame, exclude voices, and stifle innovation.
quote: "Already fully worked out solutions in childrens and commissioning they have the solution, they know what it is and this is what you've go to do. The other is collective developmen

name: Collaborative
leftDef: Collaborative: Emphasizes participatory collaboration, legitimises the role and contribution of partners and seeks to create a coalition of the willing. Focuses on combined success and achieving shared goals through building consensus, partnership working and cooperation. Creates a cooperative and collaborative environment where stakeholders work together toward common outcomes
rightDef: Competitive: Characterized by a narrow, internal focus where collaboration is limited or absent. Competitive tensions dominate, with participants and leaders prioritizing individual or organizational success over collective goals. This approach often leads to siloed efforts, personal gain, and reduced cooperation, as individuals or groups compete against each other rather than working together for the broader system.
quote: "Within B its the leaders putting their hands up saying, actually, I don't know or we've been trying to address this gap for 20 yrs and we haven't actually made any difference vers

name: System-focused
leftDef: System-Focused: Prioritizes the broader system's needs over individual organizational interests. Focus on long-term, holistic outcomes that benefit entire communities and systems. Fosters cross-boundary collaboration and shared responsibility, promote inclusivity and collective impact. Communication is open, and decisions consider system-wide implications, promoting partnerships and blurring organizational boundaries to ensure overall system success over competition or status.
rightDef: Single (sovereign)-Organization Focused: Focused on the success of individual organizations, often driven by fear of failure or the need to maintain status. Insular, short-term outputs, protecting organizational interests, and ignoring the broader system's needs. Decision-making is often self-serving, little focus on collective impact, fostering competition and siloed thinking. Communication is limited, and leaders struggle to see beyond their own organisations.
quote: "Driven to get the job done, deliver pre-determined goals and outcomes. System situations were focused on better outcomes for populations and system. Real system", "We saw the lead

name: Bottom-up
leftDef: Bottom-Up: Draws on new power and distributes leadership authority and autonomy, welcomes and supports leadership from all levels of the organisation and system. Individuals, teams, stakeholders and partners at all levels are encouraged to share their insights and contribute to decision-making processes. Leaders adopt a facilitative role, supporting team members to engage in leadership activities.
rightDef: Top Down/Command-Control: Driven by status/hierarchy and heroic leadership, leaders dominate through command & control. Leadership decisions are pre-determined by those at the top of the organisation. This leadership style is traditional, staff are told what is going to happen, how it will happen and when it will happen. These leaders focus on individual agendas and foster a culture where old power structures dominate.
quote: "Those people say I'm doing something to you rather than with you. Its quite interesting actually, if you asked people in the blue scenarios whether they feel involved in those dec

name: Shared
leftDef: Shared Decision-Making: Fosters joint accountability by involving stakeholders in shaping decisions through shared ownership and shared direction. Power is distributed, promoting democracy and encouraging leaders to give up power to ensure diverse voices are heard. Create a culture of shared decision-making. Enhances collaboration, engagement, and commitment to collective outcomes, driving mutual trust and strengthening relationships across the system.
rightDef: Individual Leader Decision-Making: Characterized by centralized authority, decisions are made by individual privileged senior leaders, minimal opportunities for sharing decision making with wider stakeholders or system partners. Individual leaders drive through decisions based on their individualised views of the world, which principally reflect only their own perspectives, biases and interests. Culture of compliance rather than engagement.
quote: "Recognising the need to do things differently, change goals to create a shared vision and plan", "Multi-stakeholder v one track agenda. On track agenda this was what happened in C

name: Relational
leftDef: Relational: Prioritises people and the power of individual and team relationships before process, focusing on building strong, authentic relationships. Active listening and self-awareness are key, encourage people-centered approaches that value individuals' contributions. Highly relational and fosters collaboration, as well as emphasising the importance of leaders establishing long-term, meaningful relationships within and across their organisations and systems.
rightDef: Positional: Relies on positional power to drive compliance and outcomes. Leaders derive their influence and authority from their position within the hierarchy and formal title. Defensive and characterized by rigid processes, where communication is one-way. Prioritize efficiency, technical expertise and specialism, as forms of control, over interpersonal dynamics. Barriers to collaboration and limiting opportunities for engagement. Focus on delivering results quickly rather than investing in relationships or collective efforts.
quote: "Highly relational interactions, relationship developing, all happened outside formal processes. Very different in D and F whereas it was very positional and process led. Everythin

name: Multi-dimensional
leftDef: Multi-Dimensional: Recognise the complexity of organisational and system challenges and issues. Embrace a holistic view that considers multiple factors; political, financial, motivational, and sustainability aspects. Leaders engage a wide range of stakeholders, facilitating collaborative efforts to tackle "wicked problems" that cannot be solved through simplistic or purely technical solutions. These leaders actively remove red lines and embrace broader perspectives and multi-faceted responses.
rightDef: Single-Issue: Focus narrowly and ignore the complexity of organisational and system challenges. Approach leadership challenges as individual, static and silo based issues. See their leadership roles as a series of disconnected actions and activities. Impact is viewed as one dimensional and lacking the complexity of organisational problems.
quote: "The system scenarios were multi-dimension and needed leadership that recognised these dimensions to be effective, political, financial, motivational, sustainability and delivery a

name: Building trust
leftDef: Building Trust: Fosters trust and emphasizes transparency, openness, and sharing. Promote open access to information, creating an environment of psychological and emotional safety, team members feel secure and informed. Focuses on relationships and consistent communication, build trust through actions. Openness fosters deeper collaboration and strengthens connections across teams, creating a high-trust atmosphere.
rightDef: Undermining Trust: Fails to build trusted relationships with followers, colleagues, stakeholders. Mutual trust and confidence is absent and leadership relationships are characterised by secrecy, command-and-control dynamics, and a focus on power. Lacks transparency, defensive and protective of power and central decision making. Erodes trust at individual, organisational and system levels.

name: Adaptive/Emergent
leftDef: Adaptive/Emergent: Accept the ambiguity and uncertainty of organisational and system environments. Lead with an adaptive mindset, foster psychological safety, promote curiosity and continuous testing and learning. Focus on teams and groups rather than individuals. They continue to adapt, grow and develop themselves through dynamic interactions and engagement with colleagues, partners and other system players. Promotes Enables discovery and evolution.
rightDef: Formal: Focus on maintaining the status quo and executing established plans without flexibility. Actively avoids the necessity for adaptive leadership, favouring a role-based perspective on organisational and system leadership requirements.

name: Other
quote: "D and F was governance heavy in their leadership culture, which functioned in quite a traditional way, verses B which was more informal in terms of approach"

name: Creating social capital
leftDef: Creating Social Capital: Recognise the power of social influence prioritise building social capital through fostering relationships, collaboration, and community engagement. Values partnership development as a social activity, creating a strong network of relationships. Leadership is fundamentally recognised as a social process. Leadership is developed through social interactions. Leaders seek to address complex system problems through the power of social interactions, social dynamics and deep partnership working.
rightDef: Building Human Capital: Emphasises individual leadership capabilities and transactional leadership. Prioritises single leadership capabilities to solve problems, overlooking the need to build social connections within teams, across the system and communities. A leader-led approach to leadership and leadership development.
quote: "So it's bringing people together in the community paradigms from different sectors and skill sets", "B was all about being socially led, developing a social interactive process wh

name: Reflective
leftDef: Reflective: Focus on continuous learning and developmental, prioritising the importance of creating knowledge and insight from experiences to support individual and wider team development. Fosters a culture that encourages curiosity and sees the benefits of making mistakes as essential opportunities for learning. This leadership actively promotes learning from failures and successes. Develop insights that contribute to personal and collective growth.
rightDef: Inward-Looking: Fails to capture and utilise opportunities for growth, focus remains on maintaining status quo rather than reflection and adaptation. Leaders have a fear of failure, leading to a reluctance to experiment or learn from mistakes, stifling innovation and improvement. Primarily concentrate on their own services or departments, neglecting the interconnectedness of the wider system.
quote: "In D and F leaders were fixated on what they saw as the prize. The approach was just look forward and keep going, there was very little reflection. Whereas the leadership model in

name: Leading without authority
leftDef: Leading Without Authority: Operate on the basis of influencing and guiding others without relying on formal power or hierarchical status. Collaboration over control, fostering collaborative environments. Relationships and shared goals instead of authority. Engage team members in shaping outcomes and decisions. Open to different perspectives and willing to adjust approaches based on collective inputs, views and ideas.
rightDef: Authority-Driven: Operate from a basis of formal power and control, reflects established hierarchies and positional power. Leaders dictate tasks and expect compliance rather than collaboration. Leaders focus on maintaining control over teams and outcomes. Little room for negotiation or shared decision-making. Their authority overshadows contributions from others.
